summary: The draft is densely cited for benchmark-subset comparators, but three paragraphs rest on thin or indirect support: the out-of-range (stronger-than-source) target motivation, the IRT/Fisher-information design foundations, and the model-assisted difference estimator.
missing_literatures: extrapolation of benchmark or ability prediction to models outside the source range
item response theory and Fisher-information item selection in adaptive testing
model-assisted difference estimation in survey sampling

rewrite_targets.reason: The introduction calls the better-than-all-sources case 'the hardest and most practically relevant' and frames the paper around it, but gives no citation showing that benchmark prediction degrades outside the source range or that evaluating new, stronger models is where savings matter. Reviewers will expect this positioning to be tied to prior evidence; the only related cite, Zhang et al., is used for data rather than for this point.
rewrite_targets.anchor_text: The hardest and most practically relevant case is a new model that is better than all sources
search_topics: benchmark performance prediction extrapolation to stronger or newer LLMs
out-of-distribution or frontier model score prediction from older model results
failure of low-rank or IRT benchmark prediction under distribution shift in model ability

rewrite_targets.reason: The 'Estimation and design tools' paragraph treats the logistic latent model and Fisher-information item selection as established, but supports them only with an NLP-leaderboard IRT paper and Kiefer's D-optimality result. The multidimensional IRT, MAP ability estimation and Fisher-information item selection foundations that the method builds on are not cited.
rewrite_targets.anchor_text: The latent model is an IRT-style logistic model fitted to a model-by-item matrix
search_topics: multidimensional item response theory logistic model
Fisher information item selection computerized adaptive testing
D-optimal design for item calibration or ability estimation in IRT

rewrite_targets.reason: The estimator that adds the mean residual of the revealed items to a model-based prediction is the classical model-assisted or difference estimator from survey sampling. The draft links it only to prediction-powered inference, which is a recent descendant. One or two foundational or bridging citations would position it correctly.
rewrite_targets.anchor_text: follows the model-assisted approach of correcting a model-based prediction with an observed-sample residual
search_topics: PPI++ or active statistical inference with model predictions and labeled sample
